# Specs generated from the Lean model

Each folder is a requirement spec with one `requirements.md`, generated from the rules in one Lean module. The acceptance criteria are in EARS notation, and the folders follow the layout Kiro reads. The rule's docstring holds the user story and the acceptance criteria; the build computes each criterion's status from the theorems and examples tagged `@[checks]` with its ID. To change a requirement, edit the docstring and rebuild.

71 acceptance criteria: 49 proven, 7 example only, 14 open, 1 not checked.

## Acceptance criteria

| ID | Criterion | Status | Checked by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ONE-001.1 | WHEN an offer is accepted THE SYSTEM SHALL create exactly one order item for each offer item. | proven | proven theorem `accept_item_per_offer_item`; example `acceptFamilyOffer` |
| ONE-001.2 | WHEN an order item is created THE SYSTEM SHALL give it one service for each passenger and flight segment of its offer item. | proven | proven theorem `accept_services_per_passenger_segment`; example `acceptFamilyOffer` |
| ONE-001.3 | WHEN an order is created THE SYSTEM SHALL give its order items distinct references. | proven | proven theorem `accept_item_ids_unique`; example `acceptFamilyOffer` |
| ONE-001.4 | WHEN an order is created THE SYSTEM SHALL mark it opened. | proven | proven theorem `accept_order_opened`; example `acceptFamilyOffer` |
| ONE-001.5 | IF a customer accepts an offer at or after its expiry instant THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject it as expired. | proven | proven theorem `accept_rejects_expired`; example `acceptFamilyAtExpiry` |
| ONE-002.1 | WHILE at least one service of an order item holds value THE SYSTEM SHALL mark the item active. | proven | proven theorem `item_active_iff`; example `paidItem` |
| ONE-002.2 | WHEN every service of an order item is cancelled or transferred and none holds value THE SYSTEM SHALL mark the item cancelled. | proven | proven theorem `item_cancelled_iff`; example `cancelledItem` |
| ONE-002.3 | WHEN at least one service of an order item is delivered and every other service is delivered or removed THE SYSTEM SHALL mark the item closed. | proven | proven theorem `item_closed_iff`; example `closedItem` |
| ONE-002.4 | THE SYSTEM SHALL give each order item exactly one status. | open | proven theorem `active_not_cancelled`; proven theorem `active_not_closed`; open theorem `item_has_one_status`; counterexample `deliveredThenTransferred`; counterexample `suspendedService` |
| ONE-003.1 | WHILE at least one service of an order holds value THE SYSTEM SHALL mark the order opened. | proven | proven theorem `order_opened_iff`; example `acceptFamilyOffer` |
| ONE-003.2 | WHEN every item of an order is closed or cancelled and every service is delivered or removed THE SYSTEM SHALL mark the order closed. | proven | proven theorem `order_closed_iff`; example `deliveredOrder` |
| ONE-003.3 | THE SYSTEM SHALL never mark an order both opened and closed. | proven | proven theorem `opened_closed_exclusive` |
| ONE-003.4 | THE SYSTEM SHALL give every order that has a service either the status opened or the status closed. | open | open theorem `order_opened_or_closed`; counterexample `expiredService` |
| ONE-101.1 | WHEN the airline confirms a REQUESTED service THE SYSTEM SHALL mark it CONFIRMED. | proven | proven theorem `confirm_marks_confirmed` |
| ONE-101.2 | WHEN payment for a CONFIRMED service succeeds THE SYSTEM SHALL mark it READY TO PROCEED. | proven | proven theorem `pay_marks_ready`; example `paidFlightDelivered` |
| ONE-101.3 | WHEN a service that is READY TO PROCEED, READY TO DELIVER or IN PROGRESS is delivered THE SYSTEM SHALL mark it DELIVERED. | proven | proven theorem `deliver_marks_delivered`; example `paidFlightDelivered` |
| ONE-101.4 | IF payment for a service has not succeeded THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL keep it out of READY TO PROCEED, READY TO DELIVER, IN PROGRESS and DELIVERED. | open | open theorem `paid_before_delivery`; counterexample `deliveredBeforePayment`; counterexample `unpaidAfterForceMajeure` |
| ONE-101.5 | WHERE the airline allows no delivery before payment and no return from UNABLE TO DELIVER to READY TO PROCEED THE SYSTEM SHALL keep a service whose payment has not succeeded out of READY TO PROCEED, READY TO DELIVER, IN PROGRESS and DELIVERED. | proven | proven theorem `paid_before_delivery_with_gate`; example `deliveredBeforePayment`; example `unpaidAfterForceMajeure` |
| ONE-101.6 | IF an event has no move from the service's delivery status in the table THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse it. | example only | example `moveTable`; example `undecidedMoves` |
| ONE-102.1 | WHEN a service that is CONFIRMED, READY TO PROCEED or READY TO DELIVER is cancelled THE SYSTEM SHALL mark it REMOVED HOLD VALUE if the airline holds its value for reuse and REMOVED if not. | proven | proven theorem `cancel_removes`; example `reusableCancellation` |
| ONE-102.2 | WHEN the value held for a REMOVED HOLD VALUE service is refunded, moved to a value store or used in a change THE SYSTEM SHALL mark it REMOVED, the only move out of REMOVED HOLD VALUE. | proven | proven theorem `held_value_only_released`; example `reusableCancellation` |
| ONE-102.3 | WHEN the consumption time limit of a service that is CONFIRMED, READY TO PROCEED or READY TO DELIVER passes before the customer claims it THE SYSTEM SHALL mark it EXPIRED. | proven | proven theorem `expire_marks_expired`; example `outcomesOfPaidFlight` |
| ONE-102.4 | WHEN the passenger's own action or inaction, such as a no-show, prevents delivery of a service that is CONFIRMED, READY TO PROCEED or READY TO DELIVER THE SYSTEM SHALL mark it NOT CLAIMED. | proven | proven theorem `no_show_marks_not_claimed`; example `outcomesOfPaidFlight` |
| ONE-102.5 | WHEN legal, regulatory or force majeure constraints prevent delivery of a service that is CONFIRMED, READY TO PROCEED or READY TO DELIVER THE SYSTEM SHALL mark it UNABLE TO DELIVER. | proven | proven theorem `unable_marks_unable`; example `outcomesOfPaidFlight` |
| ONE-102.6 | WHEN the airline or its provider fails to deliver a service that is CONFIRMED, READY TO PROCEED, READY TO DELIVER or IN PROGRESS because of its own limits THE SYSTEM SHALL mark it FAILED TO DELIVER. | proven | proven theorem `fail_marks_failed`; example `outcomesOfPaidFlight` |
| ONE-103.1 | IF a service is DELIVERED, REMOVED, EXPIRED, NOT CLAIMED or FAILED TO DELIVER THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse every event for its delivery status. | proven | proven theorem `final_refuses_all`; example `eventsAccepted` |
| ONE-103.2 | THE SYSTEM SHALL let every service that is not in a final delivery status reach one through some sequence of events. | proven | proven theorem `final_reachable`; example `unableToDeliverWayOut` |
| ONE-103.3 | WHILE an order is closed THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse every event for the delivery status of its services. | proven | proven theorem `closed_order_refuses_events`; example `closedOrderEvents` |
| ONE-103.4 | WHEN every service of an order is in a final delivery status THE SYSTEM SHALL mark the order closed. | open | open theorem `all_final_order_closed`; counterexample `failedDeliveryOrder`; counterexample `noShowOrder` |
| ONE-104.1 | WHEN the airline suspends a service that is REQUESTED, CONFIRMED, READY TO PROCEED, READY TO DELIVER, IN PROGRESS or UNABLE TO DELIVER THE SYSTEM SHALL mark it SUSPENDED and record the status it left. | proven | proven theorem `suspend_records_status`; example `fraudSuspension` |
| ONE-104.2 | WHEN the airline lifts the suspension of a service THE SYSTEM SHALL return it to the delivery status it had before it was suspended. | proven | proven theorem `resume_returns`; example `fraudSuspension` |
| ONE-104.3 | WHEN a suspended service is cancelled with none of its value kept THE SYSTEM SHALL mark it REMOVED. | proven | proven theorem `suspended_cancel_removes`; example `suspendedThenCancelled` |
| ONE-104.4 | WHILE a service is suspended THE SYSTEM SHALL move it only to the delivery status it left or to REMOVED. | proven | proven theorem `suspended_moves_back_or_removed`; example `fraudSuspension`; example `suspendedThenCancelled` |
| ONE-104.5 | WHEN any event but a suspension happens to a service that is not suspended THE SYSTEM SHALL apply the move in the delivery status table. | proven | proven theorem `step_follows_table` |
| ONE-201.1 | IF the prices, penalty and forfeited amount of a change are not all in one currency THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject the change unpriced. | proven | proven theorem `differential_rejects_mixed_currency`; example `mixedCurrencyChange` |
| ONE-201.2 | THE SYSTEM SHALL give a price differential a type code that names a collection exactly when an amount is due to the airline. | proven | proven theorem `differential_collects_iff`; example `changeWithCollection`; example `penaltyNettedOrSeparate` |
| ONE-201.3 | THE SYSTEM SHALL give a price differential a type code that names a refund or a value store exactly when an amount is due by the airline. | proven | proven theorem `differential_pays_iff`; example `cancellationWithForfeit`; example `penaltyNettedOrSeparate` |
| ONE-201.4 | WHEN the seller asks to keep the value of cancelled items for later use THE SYSTEM SHALL type the differential Reusable and set both due amounts to zero. | proven | proven theorem `respend_reusable`; example `respendCancellation` |
| ONE-201.5 | WHEN the airline prices a change or cancellation THE SYSTEM SHALL make the amount due to the airline less the amount due by the airline equal the new price, less the old price, plus the penalty, plus the forfeited amount. | open | open theorem `differential_nets`; counterexample `penaltyAboveRefund`; counterexample `respendCancellation` |
| ONE-202.1 | WHERE the penalty is netted THE SYSTEM SHALL add the penalty charged to the price difference and state the result as a single amount, due either to or by the airline. | proven | proven theorem `netted_single_amount`; example `cancellationWithForfeit`; example `changeWithCollection` |
| ONE-202.2 | WHERE the penalty is charged separately THE SYSTEM SHALL add the penalty charged to the amount due to the airline and settle the price difference on its own. | proven | proven theorem `separate_penalty_added`; example `penaltyNettedOrSeparate` |
| ONE-202.3 | THE SYSTEM SHALL give the customer the same net amount whether the penalty is netted or charged separately. | proven | proven theorem `net_same_either_way`; example `penaltyNettedOrSeparate` |
| ONE-202.4 | IF the penalty on a cancellation is larger than the refundable value of the cancelled items THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL not leave the customer owing the airline money. | open | open theorem `cancel_not_owing`; counterexample `penaltyAboveRefund` |
| ONE-203.1 | WHEN a seller asks to cancel an order for which no payment has been received THE SYSTEM SHALL cancel and remove every service of the order at once. | proven | proven theorem `unpaid_cancelled_at_once`; example `unpaidCancellation` |
| ONE-203.2 | WHEN an order is cancelled at once THE SYSTEM SHALL mark each of its items cancelled and the order closed. | proven | proven theorem `cancelled_at_once_closed`; example `unpaidCancellation` |
| ONE-203.3 | IF a seller asks to cancel an order for which any payment has been received THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL cancel it only through a cancellation offer. | proven | proven theorem `paid_needs_offer`; example `paidCancellation`; example `partlyPaidCancellation` |
| ONE-203.4 | WHEN an order with payments is cancelled through an offer THE SYSTEM SHALL not make the amount due by the airline larger than the payments received for the order. | open | open theorem `offer_within_payments`; counterexample `partlyPaidCancellation` |
| ONE-204.1 | WHEN a change keeps a service of the changed item THE SYSTEM SHALL give the new item a service with the same reference, passenger, segment and delivery status. | proven | proven theorem `change_keeps_services`; example `changeKeepingOutbound` |
| ONE-204.2 | WHEN a change keeps a service of the changed item THE SYSTEM SHALL mark the original copy transferred and leave its delivery status as it was. | proven | proven theorem `change_marks_transferred`; example `changeKeepingOutbound` |
| ONE-204.3 | WHEN a change does not keep a service of the changed item THE SYSTEM SHALL mark it cancelled and removed. | proven | proven theorem `change_cancels_others`; example `changeKeepingOutbound`; example `changeReplacingAll` |
| ONE-204.4 | WHEN a change is made THE SYSTEM SHALL keep the order's item references distinct. | proven | proven theorem `change_item_refs_unique`; example `changeReusingReference` |
| ONE-204.5 | WHEN a change is made THE SYSTEM SHALL mark the changed item cancelled. | open | open theorem `change_original_cancelled`; counterexample `changeKeepingOutbound` |
| ONE-205.1 | WHEN a seller settles a change or cancellation offer THE SYSTEM SHALL add the amount due to the airline to the order's payments and the amount due by the airline to its refunds. | proven | proven theorem `settle_adds_payments`; example `changeBalance` |
| ONE-205.2 | WHEN a seller settles a change or cancellation offer THE SYSTEM SHALL add its penalty and forfeited amount to the totals recorded on the order and lower no total recorded before. | proven | proven theorem `settle_records_penalty`; example `changeBalance` |
| ONE-205.3 | WHEN a seller settles a paid change of an order item THE SYSTEM SHALL keep the order's payments less refunds equal to the price of its live items plus the recorded penalties and forfeited amounts. | open | open theorem `change_keeps_balance`; counterexample `changeBalance` |
| ONE-401.1 | IF a selection names an item the offer does not hold THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject the selection. | proven | proven theorem `select_rejects_unknown`; example `selectingFromTrip` |
| ONE-401.2 | IF a selection leaves out an item the offer marks mandatory THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject the selection. | proven | proven theorem `select_rejects_missing_mandatory`; example `selectingFromTrip` |
| ONE-401.3 | WHEN a selection is accepted THE SYSTEM SHALL take every offer item it names and no other. | proven | proven theorem `select_takes_named_items`; example `selectingFromTrip` |
| ONE-401.4 | WHEN a selection is accepted THE SYSTEM SHALL include at least one item the offer marks mandatory. | open | open theorem `select_includes_mandatory`; counterexample `seatWithoutFlight` |
| ONE-402.1 | WHEN a create request is accepted THE SYSTEM SHALL create one order item for each item selected from each offer and none for the items left out. | proven | proven theorem `create_items_match_selection`; example `tripWithoutBag` |
| ONE-402.2 | WHEN an order is created from offers priced in one currency THE SYSTEM SHALL make the order's total price the sum of the prices of the selected items. | proven | proven theorem `create_price_eq_sum`; example `tripWithoutBag` |
| ONE-402.3 | IF any offer named in a create request has expired at the instant of the request THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject the whole request and create no order. | proven | proven theorem `create_rejects_expired`; example `oneOfferExpired` |
| ONE-402.4 | IF a create request selects no item from any offer THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject it. | proven | proven theorem `create_rejects_empty`; example `nothingSelected` |
| ONE-402.5 | WHEN an order is created THE SYSTEM SHALL be able to state its total price in a single currency. | open | open theorem `create_single_currency`; counterexample `twoCurrencies` |
| ONE-403.1 | WHEN a create request that names no offer with an order is accepted THE SYSTEM SHALL record the new order against every offer it names. | proven | proven theorem `create_once_records`; example `repeatedRequest` |
| ONE-403.2 | WHERE the airline returns the existing order for a repeated request THE SYSTEM SHALL answer a request that names an offer which already produced an order with a recorded order from one of its offers, and record no new order. | proven | proven theorem `repeat_returns_existing`; example `repeatedRequest` |
| ONE-403.3 | WHERE the airline rejects repeated requests THE SYSTEM SHALL reject a request that names an offer which already produced an order. | proven | proven theorem `repeat_rejected`; example `repeatedRequest` |
| ONE-403.4 | THE SYSTEM SHALL create at most one order from each offer. | open | open theorem `once_per_offer`; counterexample `repeatedRequest` |
| ONE-404.1 | WHEN an order is created THE SYSTEM SHALL give it version 1 and a history with no change groups. | proven | proven theorem `create_version_one`; example `versionsOfTrip` |
| ONE-404.2 | WHEN the airline applies a group of changes to an order THE SYSTEM SHALL apply the group to the order and raise its version by one. | proven | proven theorem `record_raises_version`; example `versionsOfTrip` |
| ONE-404.3 | THE SYSTEM SHALL keep an order's version one more than the number of change groups applied since it was created. | proven | proven theorem `version_counts_groups`; example `versionsOfTrip` |
| ONE-404.4 | WHEN a seller asks for an order's history THE SYSTEM SHALL return the order at version 1 and each later change group once, labelled with the version it produced. | proven | proven theorem `history_lists_each_group`; example `versionsOfTrip` |
| ONE-404.5 | WHEN a seller applies the change groups of an order's history to the order at version 1 in the order listed THE SYSTEM SHALL give the order as it is now. | open | open theorem `history_rebuilds_current`; counterexample `newestFirstHistory` |
| ONE-405.1 | WHEN a change request carries the order's current version THE SYSTEM SHALL apply the change and raise the version by one. | proven | proven theorem `current_version_applied`; example `twoSellersOneVersion` |
| ONE-405.2 | WHEN a change request carries no version THE SYSTEM SHALL apply the change. | proven | proven theorem `no_version_applied`; example `twoSellersOneVersion` |
| ONE-405.3 | IF a change request carries a version other than the order's current version THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject the change. | open | open theorem `stale_rejected`; counterexample `twoSellersOneVersion` |
| ONE-406.1 | WHILE an order has an active item THE SYSTEM SHALL keep the order accessible until 13 months after its creation. | proven | proven theorem `keep_from_creation`; example `retentionOfPaidOrder` |
| ONE-406.2 | WHILE an order has an active item and has been used THE SYSTEM SHALL keep the order accessible until 13 months after its first usage. | proven | proven theorem `keep_from_first_use`; example `retentionOfPaidOrder` |
| ONE-406.3 | WHEN every item of an order has become closed or cancelled THE SYSTEM SHALL keep the order accessible for 7 more days. | proven | proven theorem `keep_after_final`; example `deliveredOrderRetention` |
| ONE-406.4 | WHILE an order has an active item THE SYSTEM SHALL keep the order accessible. | open | open theorem `keep_while_active`; counterexample `storedValueNeverUsed` |
| OO-001.1 | IF a customer accepts an offer at or after its expiry instant THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject it as expired. | proven | proven theorem `accept_rejects_expired`; example `acceptAtExpiry` |
| OO-001.2 | IF a customer accepts an unexpired offer that has no items THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject it as empty. | example only | example `acceptEmptyOffer` |

| OO-002.2 | WHEN a ready service is cancelled THE SYSTEM SHALL mark it cancelled. | example only | example `transitionTable` |
